claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr material is a random solid solution.
The random HfNbTaTiZr solid solution has high configurational entropy and significant lattice distortion.
Short-range ordering in HfNbTaTiZr forms ordered B2-like HfTi and TiZr binary clusters.
The ordered HfTi and TiZr clusters can form percolating networks.
Thermal annealing or Monte Carlo schemes can induce the specified short-range ordering.
SRO formation requires a temperature sufficient to activate atomic diffusion.
The relevant processing temperature must remain below the bulk order-disorder transition temperature.
Ordered B2-like clusters locally regularize the lattice and reduce the variance of bond lengths and angles relative to the random state.
Reduced local lattice distortion decreases the scattering cross-section for high-frequency phonons.
A percolating ordered-cluster network creates continuous pathways for phonon transport.
Transport through the percolating network can override the scattering effects associated with point defects in the random alloy.
Exceeding the cluster percolation threshold produces a net increase in lattice thermal conductivity relative to the random alloy.
Ordering shifts the high-frequency phonon density of states toward higher frequencies.
The proposed high-frequency phonon-DOS modification corresponds to higher phonon group velocities.
Ordered regions exhibit reduced atomic displacement amplitudes or Debye-Waller factors.
Below the cluster percolation threshold, isolated ordered clusters increase scattering and reduce conductivity.
The conductivity-enhancement effect is limited to the temperature range over which B2-like order remains stable.
Monotonically decreasing thermal conductivity with increasing SRO would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe the predicted high-frequency phonon-DOS change after ordered clusters form would falsify the proposed mechanism.
